scripts.radio:
Hamjambo wasikilizaji, this is Kenya on Record. Every month, your payslip gets leaner. Every trip to the duka costs more as VAT and fuel levies squeeze your pocket dry. We are told the government needs revenue, that we must tighten our belts to build the nation.

Fair enough. But here is the number they don't say out loud on podiums: Kenya is losing an estimated 403 billion shillings every single year through illicit financial flows. That is 403 billion slipping through our fingers through corrupt deals, trade misinvoicing, tax evasion by multinational corporations, and secret offshore accounts.

To put that into perspective, 403 billion is enough to fully fund healthcare, fix broken classrooms, and service a massive chunk of our public debt without adding a single cent to your bread, fuel, or salary. The tragedy is that while ordinary citizens and mama mbogas are tracked down for every coin, the big players siphoning billions overseas face little scrutiny. Accountability cannot be a burden carried only by the poor. If we plugged the leaks, we wouldn't need to bleed the mwananchi.

Kwa kifupi kwa lugha yetu ya taifa: Kenya inapoteza shilingi bilioni mia nne na tatu kila mwaka kupitia ufisadi na ukwepaji kodi wa mashirika makubwa, huku mwananchi wa kawaida akilemewa na mzigo wa ushuru. Lazima serikali ifunge mianya hii badala ya kumkaba koo mlipakodi mdogo.
scripts.voice_note: Hey people, think about this for a minute. Every single year, Kenya loses 403 billion shillings through illicit financial flows. We are talking about massive tax evasion by multinationals, fake trade invoices, and looted public cash hidden in offshore accounts. Meanwhile, what happens back home? The government turns to you and me, raising taxes on fuel, food, and basic salaries to bridge budget deficits. It makes no sense. If our authorities put half the energy they spend taxing salaried workers and small traders into actually stopping these illegal cross-border leaks, nobody would need to hike your taxes. Let’s stop accepting the narrative that the country has no money. The resources exist—they are just leaking out into private pockets abroad. Ask your leaders today: what concrete steps are they taking to stop illicit financial flows?
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Kenya loses Sh403B yearly to illicit financial leaks while you get overtaxed. Demand leaders seal offshore tax evasion, not squeeze your pocket.
scripts.reels: Four hundred and three billion shillings. That is what Kenya loses every year to illicit financial flows—through corporate tax dodging, fake invoicing, and offshore looting. Yet every budget cycle, the state hikes taxes on your food, fuel, and salary to cover the gap. The country isn’t broke; our system is bleeding cash to the corrupt. Demand leaders seal the leaks, instead of squeezing the citizen.
